title: Delight in everything: Atik, Arich and the cord that runs from the Essence to the last particular
overview:
Chapter 24 applies the analogy of the soul's delight above. The simple delight in the Essence before the *tzimtzum*, *sha'ashuei hamelech*, is what everything lives from, the ten *sefiros* and every particular of *Atzilus*, and yet the Essence itself is higher even than that delight: it only shines through it.

The *Etz Chaim*'s *Atik* and *Arich* are the delight and the will, one essence, engraved one inside the other. *Atik* still counts as the Essence, because it begins where the self-image of *Adam Kadmon* ends; *Arich*, a will for a thing, is the head of the emanated. The delight is dressed in everything, even in *kelipa*: that is why a sin uses G-d's own delight, and why what a person enjoys clings to his soul, as stories of hell and of the *Arizal* show. In particular the *chesed* of *Atik* is in the *gulgalta*, like a father's generosity at his son's wedding, and its *gevura* in the hidden wisdom, which is why the Torah is laws. Above them, the delight before any will is tied to the Essence like a rein to a horse, and its eternity, shining into time, is *Atik Yomin*.

sections.title: Everything, before the tzimtzum and after, lives from the simple delight
sections.summary: The simple delight in the Essence before the *tzimtzum* is *sha'ashuei hamelech*, the King's delight in Himself, and the ten essential *sefiros* all come from it, as the soul's own kindness lives from its delight.

phrases.he: (כד) והנמשל מכל הנזכר לעיל למשכיל למעלה יובן
איך שבחינת עצמות התענוג הפשוט שבעצמות אור אין סוף קודם הצמצום, הוא הנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמותו, שהוא בבחינת אין סוף ממש
וגם בעשר ספירות העצמיים שהוא כתר ועד מלכות דאין סוף, הכל מבחינת העונג הפשוט שבעצמותו
על דרך משל שגם החסד העצמי שבנפש, עיקר קיומו העונג כו'

blocks.text: The simple delight in the *Atzmus* (Essence) of the *Or Ein Sof* before the *tzimtzum* (contraction) is *sha'ashuei hamelech*, the King's delight in Himself. The ten essential *sefiros*, *Keser* to *Malchus* of the *Ein Sof*, are all from it: *murkav* (composite) or *pashut* (simple), their *kiyum* (existence) comes from their *Keser*. So in the soul, the essential *chesed* (kindness) lives from the delight; that is why it is called *chafetz chesed*, a desire for kindness.
Rereading these lines, he puts the soul's essential kindness in one sentence: the main thing is that he enjoys doing good.

sections.title: The Essence is beyond even the delight; it only shines through it, all the way down
sections.summary: The *Atzmus* is higher than the simple delight and only shines through it, so "there is nothing higher than delight" is not really true. The delight in *chafetz chesed* carries the kindness down into a separate thing, to the last particular of *Atzilus*, and it is the same delight all the way.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה באמת הרי עצמות אור אין סוף מובדל גם מבחינת תענוג פשוט
phrases.en: The *Atzmus* is really higher than the actual *taanug hapashut*.

phrases.he: רק שנמשך ומאיר בבחינת העונג, כמו שעצמות הנפש תומשך אחר העונג כו'
ולזה אמר אין לך למעלה מן העונג כו'
phrases.en: That's why it said there's nothing higher than *oneg*.

blocks.text: And yet the *Atzmus* of the *Or Ein Sof* is truly separate even from the simple delight: **the *Atzmus* is really higher than the actual *taanug hapashut***. It only draws and shines in the delight, the way the essence of the soul is drawn after an *oneg* (a delight), as chapter 23 explained. **That's why it said there's nothing higher than *oneg***, and it is not really true.

In the second reading: the *Atzmus* is not the delight; even the delight of *sha'ashuei hamelech* is still not the actual self. "There is nothing higher than delight" is said because the delight is the highest of everything.

phrases.he: וכמו בבחינת חפץ חסד שבעצמות, שיש בו תענוג הפשוט
הוא נמשך ומאיר בתוספת אור עד שיורד ובא גם בדבר נבדל
שהוא בבחינת תענוג והרצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל שאחר הצמצום, להיות מקור להשתלשלות דאבי''ע
עד שיורד ונמשך בסיום הכל,
והוא גם בפרט דעשר ספירות היותר אחרון שבאצילות
phrases.en: Even in the final thing of *Atzilus*, the *oneg* is.

phrases.he: על דרך משל הנזכר לעיל בעונג הנמצא לקיום מדת הניצוח וכהאי גוונא

blocks.text: So with the *chafetz chesed* in the Essence, which holds the simple delight: because of the delight it is drawn and shines with added light, down into a *davar nivdal* (a separate thing). That delight and *ratzon kadum* (preceding will) after the *tzimtzum*, though of the Essence, is already a delight for a separate thing, the source of *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*. **Even in the final thing of *Atzilus*, the *oneg* is**, and it is all the same delight.

The second reading spells it out. He enjoys *chesed*, so he has *chesed* even in a separate thing. The same simple delight goes through the *ratzon kadum* and the *tzimtzum* to the last particular of the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus*, and it is still the delight of *sha'ashuei hamelech* coming in there. So in the trait of winning: it is *mamash* (actually) his own personal delight when he wins.

sections.title: Atik and Arich: delight and will, one essence, dressed in every sefira and around them all
sections.summary: *Atik* and *Arich* are the delight and the will, one essence, engraved one inside the other, with a third head, the delight that is not felt. That delight is dressed in every particular, even in *kelipa*, which is why a sin is a sin, and it also encompasses them all, like water running through ten ditches.

phrases.he: וזה שכתוב בעץ חיים, דעתיק יומין ואריך אנפין, שהוא התענוג והרצון, שמהות אחד הם, (ונקרא ג' רישין
דמתגלפין דא לגו מן דא כו'
phrases.en: Engraved, one inside of the other.

phrases.he: ולפעמים זה פנימי כו'
phrases.en: And you never know which one is the inside one.

phrases.he: כנזכר לעיל(ואין זה בלא זה

blocks.text: The *Etz Chaim* says that *Atik Yomin* and *Arich Anpin* are the delight and the will, one essence, not one without the other, and calls them the *gimmel rishin* (the three heads), engraved one inside the other. Delight and will make two; what is the third head? The third head is the *Radla* (the unknowable head).

blocks.title: The delight of breathing
blocks.text: The third is a delight and will that are not felt. There is a delight that is felt and one that is not, like the delight of breathing: you *mamash* don't feel it, but if, G-d forbid, it is missing, you see that it is bigger than all the other delights put together.
Sometimes this one is the inner one: **and you never know which one is the inside one**. That is the word the *Etz Chaim* uses, **engraved, one inside of the other**.

phrases.he: מלובש תוך כל ספירה וספירה בפרטי פרטות,
phrases.en: It goes all the way down to the particular *sefiros* of *Atzilus*.

phrases.he: שבלעדו אין לו קיום כלל כנזכר לעיל באריכות

blocks.text: This delight and will are *malbush* (dressed) inside every *sefira* to the last particular; without it nothing has any *kiyum* at all. **It goes all the way down to the particular *sefiros* of *Atzilus***, and really further, to a separate thing in the *sefiros* of *Beriya*, *Yetzira* and *Asiya*, and further still, into the *sefiros* of *kelipa* (the husk that conceals G-dliness).

Even in the *sefiros* of the three impure *kelipos*, the delight in those things is literally the essential delight of the *Aibershter* (the One Above, G-d). That is the whole reason a sin is a sin: you are using the *Aibershter*'s own essential delight to have this delight.

In delight there is really no difference. The line said that delight and will are one essence, in the simple and in the composite; the real point is that they are the soul itself drawn forth, and the *Aibershter*'s essential delight is Himself drawn forth. So when someone is into a delight of *kelipa*, the very essence of his soul is *mamash* being pulled after it.

phrases.he: וגם הוא מקיף את כולם
phrases.en: It's a *makif* on all of them.

phrases.he: )וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר במשל עשר חפירות זה אחר זה שהראשונה נמשכת בתוך כל חפירה וחפירה כו'
וכך אמר בזהר עבד מנא רברבא וקארי בה גרמיה חכים כו'
וכן מה שכתוב אפיק עשר תיקונין
phrases.en: *Tikkunin* means actually clothings.

phrases.he: וקרינן לון עשר ספירות כו׳)
phrases.en: And he called these clothings the ten *sefiros*.

blocks.text: And it also encompasses them all. It is *mamash* dressed in each one of them, and it is a *makif* (an encompassing light) on all of them.

blocks.title: Ten ditches and one hose
blocks.text: As explained elsewhere: ten ditches in a row, with a little channel between each. A man stands with a hose and fills the first; it overflows into the second, the second into the third, all the way to the tenth. It is not different water but *mamash* the water he put into the first. So down to the last level, the life in it is the same life of the essential delight that went into the first.

So the *Zohar* says He made great garments (he thinks *mani* means clothing) and called Himself by them wise, wise but not with a known wisdom. And He brought out ten *tikkunin*, which also means clothings, the way you fix yourself up with your clothing. **And he called these clothings the ten *sefiros***.

sections.title: Atik still counts as the world of the Ein Sof; Arich is the head of what is emanated
sections.summary: The world of the *Ein Sof* reaches down to *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon*, the end of His self-image, and that end becomes *Keser* of *Atik*, so all of *Atik* still counts as the Essence. *Arich* is the will that comes from the delight, a will for a thing, and it is the head of the emanated.

phrases.he: להיות כי בחינת עתיק יומין נחשב מסוף עולם האין סוף עדיין
לפי שעולם האין סוף נחשב עד בחינת מלכות דאדם קדמון,
שהוא בחינת אותיות וסוף מעשה שעלה במחשבה ורצון הקדום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* is the end of the *maaseh* which came up in the *ratzon kadum*.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת אחרונה שבעצמות
phrases.en: That's the last *bechina* of Himself.

phrases.he: שנעשה כתר דעתיק יומין,
phrases.en: That last thing of the self-image becomes *Keser* of *Atik*.

phrases.he: שזהו בחינת גלוי אור העונג מהעלם העונג ורצון קדום הנזכר לעיל
phrases.en: *Atik* is the revelation of the light of the *oneg* from the hidden *oneg* in the *ratzon kadum*.

phrases.he: על כן גם כתר דעתיק יומין וחכמה ובינה ומדות שבו,
phrases.en: The whole *Atik* is considered, not just the first three.

phrases.he: הכל נחשב מסוף עולם האין סוף

blocks.text: *Atik Yomin* is still counted as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*, because that world reaches down to *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon*, the letters. *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon* is the end of the *maaseh* (the deed) that came up in the *ratzon kadum*.

That is the last level of the Essence: the *Malchus* of His self-image, how He feels He should act, what He should do outside Himself. That last thing becomes *Keser* of *Atik*, the inside of the delight: what He will have delight in, since the delight follows the self-image, this and not that. So *Atik* is the revelation of the light of the delight from the delight hidden in the *ratzon kadum*.

So *Keser* of *Atik* with its *chachma*, *bina* and *middos* (emotional attributes) all count as the end of the world of the *Ein Sof*. **The whole *Atik* is considered, not just the first three**. In particular only the first three are totally not dressed in what is below; but the whole of a *sefira* is its *Keser*.

In the second reading: *Adam Kadmon* still counts as the actual *etzem* (essence), though it is external, because it is His self-image, how He will relate to the world. It is a *ratzon l'ratzon* (a will for a will): not an actual will, but how His will should be when something comes up outside. Its end, *Malchus* of *Adam Kadmon*, becomes *Keser* of *Atik*.

phrases.he: אבל בחינת אריך אנפין שהוא בחינת גלוי הרצון שבא מחמת העונג
phrases.en: That's the *ratzon* that comes because of the *oneg*.

phrases.he: להיותו נמשך ובא להתפשט למטה כו', הוא הנקרא ראש ושרש הנאצלים, שהן עשר ספירות דאצילות בכלל ובפרט

blocks.text: But *Arich Anpin* is the revelation of the will: **that's the *ratzon* that comes because of the *oneg***. He decides that he wants a certain delight, so he has a will for a certain thing. The delight, even while he is having it, is himself having it; the will is for the thing.

Though if you look closely, the will too, at any level, is still part of the *Atzmus*: you do not just want the thing, you want it for yourself. And because *Arich* is drawn down to spread below, it is called the head and root of the emanated, the ten *sefiros* of *Atzilus* in general and in particular.

sections.title: Keser in between: the emanated are separate, yet the delight in them is tied to the Essence
sections.summary: *Keser* is the *memutza*, the intermediary: it has the last level of the Essence and is the head of the emanated, whose lights are already separate. Yet the delight and will in them all come from the Essence and are tied to it like a cord: pull below and it pulls above, so what a person takes delight in clings to his soul.

phrases.he: ולזה נקרא בחינת הכתר בכלל בחינת ממוצע, שיש בו מבחינת אחרונה שבעצמות,
והוא ראש לנאצלים
phrases.en: And it's also the *rosh* of the *ne'etzalim*.

blocks.text: So *Keser* in general is called a *memutza* (an intermediary), for the delight and the will are really one thing: it has in it the last level of the Essence, and it is also the *rosh* (the head) of the *ne'etzalim*, the emanated.

phrases.he: כי אורות הנאצלים שהן בחינת גילוי ההעלם, הרי הן בבחינת נבדל מן העצמות כנזכר לעיל (באות י''ב)
וכמו על דרך משל המדות חסד וגבורה בדבר נבדל,
שבאין מכח המדות חסד וגבורה שבעצם כו'
phrases.en: Over here *sheb'etzem* means *Adam Kadmon*.

blocks.text: The emanated lights are separate from the Essence. The revelation of the will is already a separate thing: the *ratzon kadum* is still for Himself, and here it is *mamash* the will to have this thing. So *chesed* and *gevura* in a separate thing come from the power of the *middos* in the *etzem*, which here means *Adam Kadmon*, and *Adam Kadmon* comes from the *hiyuli* (raw potential) *middos*.

phrases.he: ועם כל זה בחינת התענוג והרצון שבא מן העצמות, הוא מלובש
phrases.en: The actual *oneg* and *ratzon* which comes from the *Atzmus* is *mamash* *malbush*.

phrases.he: תוך כל, להיות קיומם תמיד כנזכר לעיל
מפני ששרש זה התענוג והרצון, בעצמות אור אין סוף שנקרא שעשועי המלך בעצמו כו'
phrases.en: Because the *shoresh* of this *oneg* is directly connected, one thing connected to the other, like a *hishtalshelus* of a chain.

blocks.text: Even so, the delight and will that come from the Essence are *mamash* dressed inside everything, to keep them in existence always: it is *mamash* the essential, simple delight in the *Or Ein Sof*. For the *shoresh* (root) of this delight is in *sha'ashuei hamelech*, connected one to the other like the links of a chain.

blocks.title: Pull one end of the cord
blocks.text: It is *mamash* connected to there, like the cord in *Derech Chaim*: pull one end of the cord and the other end pulls. If there is such a delight in *sha'ashuei hamelech*, that is the delight that comes out in the particular *sefiros* of *Atzilus*; that is what pulls. And the other way: pull on this thing in *Atzilus*, and it pulls upstairs.

This is exactly what chapter one of *Derech Chaim* is about. It goes all the way down to here: when a Jew pulls down here, either way, even into the impure *kelipa*, it pulls all the way to the top and makes a blemish upstairs. As it says, "it is pure": up above there is no blemish, and the blemish can only be in the intermediate levels. But it is affected all the same.

blocks.title: Near-death experiences: the beginning of hell
blocks.text: The soul is *mamash* affected. He can't remember where he read it, but the Frierdiker Rebbe (the previous Rebbe) explains how hell works: it is imprinted on the soul. People tell of near-death experiences: you go up, it is so beautiful, all your buddies come, it is like being in heaven. No, he says, that is the beginning of hell. They don't know what comes next, because most of them didn't die all the way. Next the angels start singing "Holy, holy, holy", and he wants to run with the angels. But everything imprinted on his soul holds on to him (the *mitzvos* are imprinted on the air of paradise and the sins on the air of hell), his mother and father, all the wonderful memories. All of a sudden he realizes: "Wait a minute, I'm not in heaven, I'm in hell." And that is the normal stuff.

blocks.title: The Arizal and the rich man's tikkun
blocks.text: Then there is the bad stuff. A rich man came to the *Arizal* (Rabbi Isaac Luria), basically trying to scam him. The *Arizal* said, "Don't you need a *tikkun* (a rectification)?" "What do I need a *tikkun* for?" "For the shiksa you went with." "What do you mean? I never went with no shiksa." The *Arizal* told him that whatever woman you go with gets connected to you; he brought her out of the man's body and showed him that she was actually holding on to him. The man fainted.

sensitivity.reason: The story's dialogue uses "shiksa", a slur for a non-Jewish woman.
sensitivity.publishable: Then there is the bad stuff. A rich man came to the *Arizal* (Rabbi Isaac Luria), basically trying to scam him. The *Arizal* said, "Don't you need a *tikkun* (a rectification)?" "What do I need a *tikkun* for?" "For the non-Jewish woman you went with." "What do you mean? I never went with no non-Jewish woman." The *Arizal* told him that whatever woman you go with gets connected to you; he brought her out of the man's body and showed him that she was actually holding on to him. The man fainted.

blocks.text: Everything you see and everything you do holds on to you. How? Through the delight, and the delight is consciousness: the delight he had in it. That is why Rabbeinu HaKadosh said he never enjoyed this world even with his small finger. And the beating in the grave, *gilgul* (reincarnation) and hell are all to take that off your soul.

blocks.title: One look from the Frierdiker Rebbe
blocks.text: As for fooling the Rebbe: an old Lubavitcher told how he became a Lubavitcher Chassid. He used to go to the *misnagdishe* yeshivos (of the opponents of Chassidism) and was looking for a Rebbe. He went to all the *Rebbelech* (little rebbes) and tested them with questions in Talmud, and he had given up: "Nobody knows nothing." He meant to become a businessman, as was the way then. His Lubavitcher friends talked him into going for *yechidus* (a private audience) with the Frierdiker Rebbe. In those days *yechidus* after a *farbrengen* (a Chassidic gathering) was like dollars: a note or a blessing, and the next man. In the corridor he was pushed so hard he thought his legs would come off. What am I doing here? But once you're in that push, there is no way out.

blocks.title: One second
blocks.text: Around the bend he could see the Rebbe, and the Rebbe looked up at him for one second. The Frierdiker Rebbe was often hidden, but now and then, he says, people used to faint. To this day, telling it, the man trembles and turns white. He almost fainted, never went in, and stood where he was until the Rebbe left. Three weeks later was *Yud Shevat* (the tenth of Shevat), so that was his one time with the Frierdiker Rebbe, and that one second fixed him up forever. So you are not going to scam the Rebbe.

לולי התענוג שבו אין לו קיום כו'
phrases.en: Doesn't have a *kiyum* at all.

phrases.he: והעדר אור העונג הוא בחינת העדר אור מציאותם כו'
phrases.en: If there's no *oneg*, the *midda* does not have an existence at all.

phrases.he: ודי למבין.

blocks.text: It is *mamash* the soul itself that is drawn after every delight. **This shows that the *oneg* is what fills up the actual *midda*, even down to a desire for an ice cream**. So here too, the particular *middos* are connected all the way up to *sha'ashuei hamelech*.

So the particular delight in each particular light is its main existence, down to *Malchus*, which is *hisnasus* (rising above): **if there's no *oneg*, the *midda* does not have an existence at all**.

sections.title: In particular: the lower seven of Atik in Arich, and a kindness that can turn the will
sections.summary: In general *Atik* is the Essence and *Arich* the world; in particular only the first three of *Atik* are the Essence, and its lower seven are dressed in *Arich*, its *chesed* in the *gulgalta*, the very will. A man at his son's wedding, in his delight, does kindness for everyone and can even turn a will of judgement into kindness.

phrases.he: וכל זה דרך כלל
phrases.en: All this is in general.

phrases.he: אבל דרך פרט, הנה רק בחינת ג׳ ראשין דעתיק יומין נחשב מבחינת העצמות
אבל ז׳ תחתונים שבו מלובש בגלגלתא דאריך אנפין
חסד דעתיק יומין בגלגלתא וגבורה במוחא סתימאה כו'
וזהו המתנשא מימות עולם כו'

blocks.text: **All this is in general**: in general *Atik* is part of the *Atzmus*, and *Arich* is connected to the world. In particular, only the first three of *Atik* are counted as the Essence; its lower seven are dressed in the *gulgalta* (the skull) of *Arich Anpin*: the *chesed* of *Atik* in the *gulgalta*, its *gevura* in the *mocha stima'a* (the hidden brain). That is "exalted above the days of the world."

After beginning the chapter again, the class argues over whether it has learned it. Rabbi Markel is sure it has: he remembers the *chesed* of *Atik* dressed in the *gulgalta*, which he once gave as a wedding speech, and the talk of time being eternal in *Atik*, and says the tapes, which are labelled, will show it. Then he sums the chapter up: in general *Atik* is the inner and *Arich* the outer; in particular the *chesed* of *Atik* is in the *gulgalta*, its *gevura* in the *mocha stima'a*, down to *Malchus* of *Atik* in *netzach* of *Arich*. The text here only says "etc."; elsewhere, he recalls, it puts *Malchus* in *netzach*, *hod*, *yesod* and *Malchus*, but really it is *netzach*.
blocks.outOfPlace: From the end of class 037, after the second reading broke off.

phrases.he: כידוע, להיות כי התהוות עיקר הרצון מן התענוג, הוא רק מבחינת המדות שבתענוג
כמו מן החסד שבתענוג

blocks.text: For the will comes about from the delight only through the *middos* in the delight, as from the *chesed* in the delight. Here "exalted above the days of the world" means that the first three of *Atik* are higher than the *middos* of *Atik*. In different places the days of the world mean different things, but it is all the same *inyan* (matter).

phrases.he: על דרך משל, כאשר אדם בעונג בשמחת חתונת בנו וכהאי גוונא, אז יטיב רב חסדו לכל
phrases.en: He has the great *taanug* and then he'll do a lot of *chesed*.

phrases.he: מצד התענוג שמרומם את נפשו
phrases.en: Because of the great *taanug* that he's having.

phrases.he: (מטעם הנזכר לעיל)
ואז יפעלו ממנו כל רצון
phrases.en: At that time, that's a good time.

phrases.he: דהיינו להפוך גם מרצון של דין לחסד

blocks.title: The father at his son's wedding
blocks.text: A man at the joy of his son's wedding: **He has the great *taanug* and then he'll do a lot of *chesed*** for everyone, because the delight lifts his soul. That is called the *chesed* of the delight.

Then any will can be had from him. **At that time, that's a good time**, as with a king: then you can ask him to commute a sentence, for a pardon. Even a will of *din* (judgement) can be turned into kindness, as when Achashverosh gave the provinces relief from taxes and the like.

skip.note: Class 037 goes from line 43 (w1240) to line 45 (w1270) without reading this line.

phrases.he: וזהו דוגמא להבין איך שבחינת חסד דעתיק יומין מלובש בגלגלתא כו'

blocks.text: That is the example for how the *chesed* of *Atik* is dressed in the *gulgalta*, in the *etzem haratzon* (the essence of the will): the *chesed* of *Atik* can change the very will from a will of *din* to a will of *chesed*. That can only be done from higher than the line of right and left, so the *chesed* is dressed higher, in the *gulgalta* itself.

sections.title: Gevura in the hidden wisdom: why chachma is judgement and the Torah is laws
sections.summary: The *gevura* of the delight, which limits it to this and not that, is dressed in the hidden *chachma* of *Arich*, the hidden reason of the will. So the old books of Kabbala call *chachma* judgement, a will that follows wisdom is exact, and the Torah, from that higher wisdom, is many laws.

phrases.he: ובחינת גבורה, שהוא בחינת הדין, בהיפך לעונג, הוא מלובש בחכמה סתימאה דאריך אנפין, שהוא טעם כמוס לרצון
שזהו לדקדק ברצון, שיהיה באופן זה דוקא ולא באופן אחר כו'
phrases.en: To be *medakdek* to want this and not to want that.

blocks.text: And *gevura*, judgement, the opposite of delight, is dressed in the *mocha stima'a* of *Arich Anpin*, the hidden reason for the will. It is the *gevura* of the delight that gives the delight limits: he will enjoy this and won't enjoy that. So in the *mocha stima'a* is the exactness **to want this and not to want that**.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בספרי הקבלה שהראשונים גזרו אומר על החכמה שהיא בבחינת דין
phrases.en: In the old *sifrei Kabbala*, what they're saying about *chachma*, that it's *bivchinas din*.

phrases.he: שכאשר הרצון בא על פי חיוב החכמה, בא בדקדוק וצמצום, כך ולא כך
phrases.en: When the *ratzon* comes according to the *sechel*, there's a *dikduk*: it should come like this and not like that.

blocks.question: The old books of Kabbala say that *chachma* is *din*, and everywhere else *chachma* is *chesed*. Which one is it?
blocks.text: Both. The revealed *chachma* is *chesed*, because it comes out of the *chesed* of *Arich*; but the *chachma stima'a* (the hidden wisdom) of *Arich* is *din*.
When you're smart and the will follows the *sechel* (intellect), it comes exact and contracted: it **should come like this and not like that**. You don't just want anything you want.

phrases.he: ועל כן על פי משפט התורה,
דאורייתא מחכמה עילאה כו',
phrases.en: When it says *Oraisa* comes from *chachma*, it's not just from *chachma*, it's from *chachma ila'a*, meaning from *chachma* of *Arich*.

phrases.he: יש דינים רבים
phrases.en: The whole Torah is with a whole bunch of *dinim*.

blocks.text: Therefore by the law of the Torah there are many laws. The Torah comes not just from *chachma* but from *chachma ila'a* (the higher wisdom): the *chachma* of *Arich*, the *chachma stima'a*. So **the whole Torah is with a whole bunch of *dinim***. It says the Torah was given "from the mouth of the Might": the *chachma stima'a* comes from the *gevura* of *Atik*.
The main thing of the Torah is the 613 *mitzvos*, so much so that Rashi's first question is why the Torah starts with *Bereishis*. Start with *Vayikra*, with the laws; what do you need stories for?

sections.title: Above wisdom: the mercy that bears sin, and the delight before any will
sections.summary: The thirteen attributes of mercy, from above *chachma*, can bear a sin, which the law of the Torah cannot; the three heads of *Atik* all the more. They are the delight as it is in itself, before any will is born, the source of all delights, tied to the Essence the way a rein is tied to a horse.

phrases.he: מה שאין כן הארת י''ג מדות הרחמים מלמעלה מחכמה שברצון כו',
שנושא עון וכו'
phrases.en: It can nullify an *avon*.

phrases.he: ומכל שכן מבחינת ג׳ ראשין דעתיק יומין שבלתי מלובש בנאצלים
phrases.en: And certainly if it can be like that from the *gulgalta*, so the *gimmel rishin* of *Atik*, which is even higher than that.

blocks.text: But the light of the thirteen attributes of mercy comes from above the *chachma* in the will, and it bears sin. (Has the class reached that part yet? No, that comes later.) Though they come out lower, from the arrangement of the beard of *Arich*, their source is higher, the *gulgalta* and higher still. Therefore **it can nullify an *avon*** (a sin), where the Torah says that if there is a sin there is a punishment.

**And certainly if it can be like that from the *gulgalta*, so the *gimmel rishin* of *Atik*, which is even higher than that**, and totally not dressed in the emanated, can certainly turn things around and bear sin.

phrases.he: והוא בחינת העונג כמו שהוא בעצמו
שעדיין לא נולד ממנו רצון כלל,
phrases.en: The *taanug* before the *ratzon* actually came out of it to have a *ratzon* for something.

phrases.he: רק עתיד להיות ממנו כל רצון כו'
phrases.en: But the *ratzon* is nonetheless inherent in it.

phrases.he: והוא נחשב מעצמות התענוג הפשוט הכללי
שהוא מבחינת מקור כל התענוגים שבעצמות אור אין סוף

blocks.text: The three heads of *Atik* are the delight as it is in itself, before any will is born from it: **the *taanug* before the *ratzon* actually came out of it to have a *ratzon* for something**. Every will is still to come from it, and the will is nonetheless inherent in it. They count as the essence of the simple, general delight, from the source of all delights in the *Atzmus* of the *Or Ein Sof*.

*Atik* is connected directly, like a rope: that is the whole of *hishtalshelus* (the chain of descent). At every level down he says, "Until here it's *mamash* the *Atzmus*," and then at the next one, here too. Really it is one straight line from the top to the bottom, and that the chain has many rings makes no difference. As chapter one of *Derech Chaim* says, pull one end and you pull the other.

blocks.title: The rein of a horse
blocks.text: It is in the laws of acquisition too: handing over the rein. Put the rein of a horse into the other man's hand, and he acquires the horse if he just pulls it. He doesn't pull the horse; he pulls the rein, and pulling the rein he pulls the horse. So when a person pulls all the way down here, he is pulling not only the rope but whoever is connected to it on the other side, all the way to the *Atzmus*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב כי עמך מקור חיים,
phrases.en: The *makor chaim* is the *taanug*.

phrases.he: מקור כל התענוגים שברצון קדום כו'
phrases.en: A *makor* of all *taanugim* which come out in the *ratzon kadum*.

blocks.text: "For with You is the source of life": the source of life is the delight. Not "You are" but "with You", because the *Atzmus* is higher than the delight, though very close. The delight pulls the *Atzmus* as the rein pulls the horse, but the rein is not *mamash* the horse. The delight below pulls the soul's essence and is tied to the delight above, and that to the *Aibershter*, the source of all delights in the *ratzon kadum*.

sections.title: Atik Yomin: the eternity of the Essence shining into time
sections.summary: The *ratzon kadum* is *Atika d'Atikin* at the top and *Atik Yomin* at the end, from the word for old age: the eternity of the Essence shining down the line into time, so that time in *Atik* is infinite. In the Essence itself there is no old age and no time at all.

phrases.he: ונקרא עתיקא דעתיקין בכללות הכל כו'
ונקרא עתיק יומין
phrases.en: The end of the line is called *Atik Yomin*.

phrases.he: כמו שכתוב בדניאל, ועתיק יומין יתיב כו', מלשון זקנה
שהוא בחינת נצחיות דעצמיות אור אין סוף
phrases.en: The everlastingness of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*.

phrases.he: כשבא ומאיר למטה בהשתלשלות דקו וחוט כו'
phrases.en: When it comes in the *hishtalshelus* of *Kav v'chut* to be *meir* in *Atik*, it's called infinite time.

blocks.text: This *ratzon kadum* is called *Atika d'Atikin* (the Ancient of the Ancients) in its whole. **The end of the line is called *Atik Yomin***; the beginning is *Atika d'Atikin*, and *Keser* of *Atzilus*, *mamash* the same thing, is also called *Atik Yomin*: the beginning and the end of it. As it says in Daniel, "and the Ancient of Days sat": from the word for old age. Here it is from old age; before, it was from "moving mountains".
It is the eternity of the *Atzmus Or Ein Sof*: when it comes down the *Kav v'chut* (the line and the thread) to shine in *Atik*, it is called infinite time.
Not fifteen billion years: an infinity of time. "So now we can see that the universe is infinite."

Everywhere it says lower and lower: fifteen billion years is in *Zeir Anpin*; lower, in the *middos* of *Malchus* of *Atzilus*, it is seven thousand years; a day of *Beriya* is a hundred years, a day of *Yetzira* ten, and all the way down a day of *Asiya* is one year. But in *Atik* it is infinite: even a second in *Atik* is infinite down here. That is why it is called *Atik*.

phrases.he: אבל בעצמותו ממש,
phrases.en: But higher than *Atik*.

phrases.he: מי איכא זקנה קמי קודשא בריך הוא כו'
phrases.en: Who can say *zikna* before the *Aibershter*?

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ועד בחלופי אתוון דאחד
phrases.en: *Va'ed*, meaning forever, is a *chiluf osiyos* of *Echad* of before the *tzimtzum*.

phrases.he: פשוט עצמו
שעצמות אור אין סוף שלמעלה מן הזמן דימי קדם כו',
phrases.en: Of *Atzmus Or Ein Sof* that is higher than the *zman* of *yemei kedem* of *Atik*.

phrases.he: כשמאיר בזמן, אז הזמן גם כן נצחי כו'
phrases.en: When it lights up in the time of *Atik*, then the time of the world, our time of this universe, is also infinite.

phrases.he: ואז נקרא עתיק יומין כו'
phrases.en: And then it's called *Atik Yomin*.

phrases.he: ודי למבין:
phrases.en: And that is enough for us to understand.

blocks.text: But in His Essence itself, higher than *Atik*: **who can say *zikna* before the *Aibershter*?** *Zikna* is old age, and there you can't even say time; you can't even say *Atik*.

As explained elsewhere on *va'ed*, "forever". Here *va'ed* is *Atik*, and it is an exchange of the letters of *Echad* (One), the One before the *tzimtzum*. Elsewhere *va'ed* is the lower one, as with *yichuda ila'a* and *yichuda tata'a* (the higher and the lower unity) in general; but the *va'ed* he means here is *Atik*, and the *Echad* is the one before which there is no old age.

The Essence of the *Or Ein Sof* is above the time of *yemei kedem* (the days of old), which here are the days of *Atik*; the days of the world are *Atzilus* (later he uses *yemei kedem* for other things). When the Essence shines into time, the time of *Atik*, then the time of the world, our time in this universe, is also infinite, and then it is called *Atik Yomin*. **And that is enough for us to understand.**

reviewQuestions.question: Why is "there is nothing higher than delight" not really true, and what then does the delight do for the Essence?
What are the three heads of *Atik*, and how does the delight of breathing explain the third?
If the delight in *kelipa* is the *Aibershter*'s own delight, why is a sin a sin?
How does a father at his son's wedding show why the *chesed* of *Atik* must be dressed in the *gulgalta*?
Why do the old books of Kabbala call *chachma* judgement, and what does that say about the Torah?
What do the cord and the rein of a horse show about the delight below and the Essence above?

notes.text: Class 036 is shared with chapter 23: only its words 1979-4184 are on this chapter and cited here.

Line 44 is not read in either class (037 goes from line 43 at w1240 to line 45 at w1270). His remark that the change from din to chesed "can only be done when you're higher than the actual line of right and left" (037 w1304-1319) carries the line's idea; it is in the block on line 45.

After finishing the chapter, class 037 begins it again by mistake (w2939) and rereads lines 1-19 with a few comments. Those comments are recap blocks under lines 1-4, 5-12 and 17-20 (outOfPlace); the rereading of lines 13-19 that adds nothing is omitted as reading. Then the class argues whether it has learned the chapter (w3580-3908), and Rabbi Markel sums it up; that is a recap under lines 33-37.

The transcript has no speaker labels; from the context it is Rabbi Markel who insists they did the chapter ("I'll do it again, I don't care", "look in your tapes"). In that argument he remembers things not on these two tapes: a simchas tenaim, his speech at a wedding on the chesed of Atik in the gulgalta, and "we were talking about what's his name, Aryeh Kaplan" in connection with time being eternal in Atik (037 w3585-3689). The class on time in 037 (w2470-2634) does not mention Kaplan. Perhaps an earlier telling of the chapter was not taped, or he is thinking of another class. Aryeh Kaplan's name is left out of the block; the reviewer may want it in.
The Arizal story is cut by the tape flip: its block cites 036 w4092-4175 and then 037 w2-56. The second audio entry is the continuation of the same story, not a second telling.

He says Rashi's first question is why the Torah does not "start with Vayikra"; Rashi (on Genesis 1:1) asks why it does not start from "This month shall be for you" (Exodus 12:2). The block keeps his words.
Line 46: he reads "מוחא סתימאה" where the text has "חכמה סתימאה"; he treats them as the same (037 w1336-1352, w1394-1430).
Line 59: he says "before he said מלשון מעתיק הרים" (037 w2456-2469) without saying where; left as said.

The near-death story: he "can't remember where I read this", from the Frierdiker Rebbe; left as he said it. In the Frierdiker Rebbe story the old Lubavitcher's stutter is left out of the text (a personal detail of an identifiable man that the point does not need).
Line 13: his English for "ולפעמים זה פנימי" (w2402-2411) comes before his English for "דמתגלפין דא לגו מן דא" (w2420-2425), so the phrases' audio runs out of order.
The aside on the age of the universe (037 w2509-2533) is not flagged: it states his position on time in Atik and says nothing against scientists. A reviewer may want to flag it.
